out.rationale: The authors state that their theoretical relaxation (average-case rather than adversarial robustness) is consistent with the empirical observation in Burns et al. and others that weak-to-strong gains occur without adversarial training. The agreement is between a theorem's assumptions and an empirical pattern, so SUPPORTS rather than REPLICATES.
out.scope: proposed SUPPORTS: Whether weak-to-strong generalization needs adversarially robust students; the agreement holds for students trained without adversarial training, with theory on one side and experiments on the other

text: The authors extend their weak-to-strong error bounds (Theorems 4.1 and 4.2) to student classifiers that are only robust on average, under a robust-expansion assumption (Theorem 4.3). They say this generalization matters because it matches empirical results, including Burns et al. [10], that adversarial training and adversarial robustness are not required for weak-to-strong generalization to occur.
title: Lang et al.'s average-case-robust W2S bounds match Burns et al.'s W2S without adversarial training
